bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/archive.rs (ByteStream, compress_to, compress_to_threaded, decompress_from, compress_file, compress_directory, expand), springboard/sdk/src/compression.rs (encode_buffer_threaded), springboard/src/files/zip.rs (create, extract), springboard/src/shell/store/install.rs (read_tar, index_tar, extract_from), springboard/render/src/cg/pdf/inflate.rs
summary: BifrOSt has an app-facing archive module in the SDK: ZIP folders and single files, raw DEFLATE for buffers, strings and byte streams, a thread-count option, a custom BFEA encrypted wrapper, and (2026-10-19) the BifrOSt archive format BAR1 in bifrost_app::archive_format: attributes, directory pack and extract with path-traversal protection and size limits, Deflate, LZ4 or LZMA payloads, and signed and sealed forms. Tar reading serves app package install. The Apple Archive container byte format, its stream protocols and its encrypted archive profiles are not present.

features.feature: Compressing and extracting file system directories

features.bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/archive.rs (compress_directory, expand); springboard/sdk/tests/parity_sdk-tests-20.rs; springboard/sdk/src/archive_format.rs (pack_directory, archive_directory, extract, extract_archive)
features.note: ZIP folder trees through the SDK archive module and the Files app (ZIP format; its members keep the zipped folder name, so expanding nests the tree one level deeper). Built 2026-10-19: bifrost_app::archive_format packs a folder into a BifrOSt archive (BAR1) with relative paths, sorted entries, links recorded and never followed, mode, owner, times and extended attributes kept, and Limits on entries (1,000,000), payload (1 GiB) and attributes; extract refuses unsafe paths and links, never writes through a link or over a file, validates every entry before writing, and sets folder modes last. Gap: not the reference container; the Files app and the Archive Utility still write ZIP, and a tree is held in memory (bounded by the limit), not streamed. features.apple: ArchiveHeader; file ownership, permissions, flags, times, extended attributes
features.bifrost: springboard/src/shell/store/install.rs (TarEntry, read_tar, index_tar); springboard/sdk/src/archive_format.rs (Header, Entry, Kind, peek)
features.note: Tar entries keep the path, mode, directory flag, contents offset and size, and the reader refuses unsafe paths, links, pax headers, duplicates and bad checksums (springboard/tests/parity_sdk-tests-12.rs); the tar path keeps no ownership, times or extended attributes. Built 2026-10-19: the BAR header keeps kind (file, folder, link), path, mode, uid, gid, modification time (seconds and nanoseconds), size and extended attributes per entry, plus a count, codec, payload length and SHA-256 in the file header (peek reads them without decompressing). Extraction restores mode, times, optional ownership (preserve_ownership, needs privilege) and extended attributes (counted when the file system has none). Not kept: file flags, access control lists, creation time. features.bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/encrypted_archive.rs (BFEA v1 wrapper over ChaCha20-Poly1305); springboard/sdk/tests/parity_sdk-rest-05.rs; springboard/sdk/src/archive_format.rs (sign, verify, encode_sealed, decode_sealed, encode_signed_sealed, decode_signed_sealed)
features.note: BFEA v1 seals caller-provided archive bytes with ChaCha20-Poly1305 and authenticates its header; host tests cover round-trip, wrong-key, tampering and version errors. Built 2026-10-19: archive_format seals a whole BAR archive in one call (encode_sealed, decode_sealed), signs one with ML-DSA (sign, verify: a BARS container, context bifrost-archive/v1, refuses a different key, any changed byte, a cut signature and an oversized signature length), and does both, signing first so the signature is hidden (encode_signed_sealed, decode_signed_sealed; an unsigned sealed archive is refused by the signed reader). Gap: this is not the Apple Encrypted Archive format or its profiles; there is no key derivation, no public-key or password profile, and keys and their storage are the caller's. Tests: archive_format.rs a_signed_archive_verifies_and_any_change_does_not, a_sealed_archive_opens_only_with_its_key, signed_then_sealed_needs_both_keys. Not compiled or run in this round. Midget check: on Titan build the SDK unit-test binary with `cargo test --offline --profile fast -p bifrost-app --lib --no-run`, copy the executable it prints to Midget with `scp`, and run `ssh midget ./<that executable> archive_format::tests::a_signed --test-threads 1`; every test passes.

gaps: BAR1 is not the Apple Archive container (AAR) byte format, field keys or stream protocols; the Files app and the Archive Utility still write ZIP
File flags, access control lists and creation time are not kept in archives; extended attributes, owner, mode and times are
No Apple-compatible encrypted archive profiles and no key derivation; sealing and signing take caller-held keys
A BAR tree is held in memory per archive (bounded by Limits), entries are not streamed one at a time
Multithreaded compression covers byte streams and BAR payloads; the Files app zip writer runs as a single background job
No optimal parsing in the DEFLATE encoder, so output is larger than a full zlib encoder
